1.1 Central idea

The supplied parent is close to a nonsmooth local optimum of the exact, finite-support correlation objective. The previous methods primarily move one coordinate pair or one direct linearization direction at a time. The new primary idea is to optimize the full-dimensional feasible variable with a controlled sequence of smooth minimax surrogate problems, followed by an acceptance gate using the exact evaluator.

For each feasible current h, solve or nearly solve

    minimize_t  F_T(h + d)

where T is a smoothing parameter and

    F_T(h) = dx * [ max_k C_k(h) +
                     T * log(sum_k exp((C_k(h)-max_j C_j(h))/T)) ].

Here C_k(h) is the unweighted finite correlation coefficient at lag k, generated exactly by
`np.correlate(h, 1.0-h, mode="full")`, and dx = 2/n. The smoothing functional is the log-sum-exp upper/lower envelope approximation of the max; as T -> 0 it converges to the true objective. A full nonlinear programming method, SLSQP, is used inside this smoothed model. SLSQP can move many coordinates simultaneously under the simplex-like [0,1]/sum constraints. Every proposed h is then repaired to the exact feasible set and accepts only after re-evaluation of the original nonsmooth evaluator

    C5(h) = max_k correlation_k(h) * (2/n).

This is materially different from earlier pair-only or active-lag linearized LP directions: the primary direction is a full multidimensional minimization of a smooth approximation of the actual nonsmooth objective, using a convex/nonconvex NLP solver, not a collection of many two-coordinate polynomial line searches.

A lower-score point at this precision needs several near-maximal lags to rotate together. Single pair moves can fail to decrease the objective whenever one pair move raises at least one of several active correlation lags.
